title: kbs commit leaves event files untracked when project/events is not gitignored
description: Reported by the Biblicus session 2026-10-19 (kbs 0.35.0 Rust, Papyrus worktree on develop): after kbs comment PPY-c32c35 and kbs close PPY-c32c35, kbs commit printed 'Committed project/issues' and committed only the issue JSON; the two event files the same commands wrote under project/events/ stayed untracked and had to be added by hand. Help says 'Commit project/issues changes to git'. The Kanbus repo itself gitignores project/events/ (so only issues are committed there), while Papyrus does not, so the behavior depends on an undocumented per-repo choice. Decide one way (no-fallback policy): either events are part of board history (kbs commit stages project/issues and project/events, kbs init does not ignore events) or they are local-only (kbs init writes the ignore rule and doctor warns when events are tracked or unignored). Then spec it in features/ and make Rust and Python identical. Related: repo hygiene sub-task under kbs-7410f7c6 also asks whether project/events should be tracked.
